title: [2026.10.14] Patch Notes: Weapon Swing Speeds and Monster Movement
text:
Combat
• Every weapon now has its own swing speed. Daggers and fists are the fastest at 0.8 seconds a swing, swords and wands take 1 second, and a sniper is the slowest at 1.4 seconds.
• Bare hands swing once a second. Before, everything swung every 0.6 seconds, so fights are slower.
• AGI, DEX, your ring, leather armour and buffs speed your swings up exactly as before.

Movement
• Shoes no longer give movement speed. Only buffs and slows change how fast you move.
• Walking, running and sprinting are a little slower than before.
• The camera no longer zooms out as far: the furthest view is two thirds of what it was.

Monsters
• Every monster now moves at its own speed. Slimes, snails and mushrooms are slow; mice, bats and raccoons are fast.
• Shootling and Canewick never move. They shoot from where they stand, and cannot be pushed or pulled.
• Shootling now carries a Sniper.
• Flutterby and Crawlet wear weaker gear and are easier to fight.
• Flutterby Scale Dust and Crawlet Cocoon no longer drop.

title: [2026.10.13] Patch Notes: Gear Drops and Creature Materials
text:
New: Gear Drops
• Gear is no longer forged. Every creature can drop a piece of what it wears: its weapon, or its head, body, shoes or garment piece.
• A dropped piece comes with a rarity. Ordinary creatures drop Common, Uncommon and Rare pieces, elites drop Epic ones, and shadows drop Legendary ones.
• The rarer a piece is, the more every fold on it is worth.
• Every weapon is wielded by ordinary creatures, by an elite and by one shadow, and every shadow now wears a full set of armour.

New: Creature Materials
• Creatures no longer drop gold. Every creature now drops a material that only it has; sell it at any shop.
• Some creatures also carry a second, rarer material with a coloured name, from Uncommon up to Legendary.
• An elite drops its material in several piles on every kill, and nothing an elite drops is picked up automatically.

Crafting
• Folding now takes Temper Dust and quenching takes Quench Oil, whatever the piece is made of. The old metals, cloths and leathers are gone.
• Every creature drops Temper Dust and Quench Oil. Harder creatures drop more.
• Recycling a piece gives back half the Temper Dust, Quench Oil and gold its folds and quenches took. Folds made at Raw give nothing back.
• The smith, the loom and the tannery fold, quench, ink and recycle. They no longer make gear.

Items & Shops
• Healing Potions and Mana Draughts now come in five sizes each: Minor, plain, Greater, Superior and Grand. The Tool Dealer sells all ten.
• Potions, Fly Wings, Butterfly Wings and Antidotes are bought from the Tool Dealer and no longer drop from creatures.
• Each creature now drops one find of its own, by its element: Fire, Water, Earth and Wind creatures drop their element's converters, and the others drop a food.
• Foods now last 5 minutes. New food: Sage Stew, which raises magic attack.
• Shops no longer buy foods or converters, and pay far less for gear, Ink and Salt.
• Your purse can now hold far more gold.

Combat
• Every creature and elite now wears a full set of gear and a weapon, and its stats are built for that weapon.
• A creature's gear decides how hard it is, whatever its level: the rarer the thing it drops and the harder it is to find, the better its gear.
• Better-geared creatures pay more experience, and their materials sell for more.
• When several players fight one creature, the one who did the most owns its loot, and the experience is shared by what each did: damage, being chased, healing others, the first hit and the last.

New Characters
• A new character starts wearing a Sword, a Chainmail and Iron Sabatons, and the first tutorial teaches folding them.
• All characters and stored items were reset for this update.

Saved Characters
• Saving a character that never fights now pays gold and some of its creature's material.

title: [2026.10.12] Patch Notes: Auto-Combat, the Keeper and the New Bag
text:
New: the Bag
• Your bag is now a grid of boxes, like the hotbar: each item by its name, a stack with its count. A tab shows all 24 of its boxes, so you can see how full it is.
• Sort by Name, Held or Rarity; with no sort chosen, things stay in the order they arrived, newest at the end.
• Double-click to use, wear or merge. Drag a box onto another to swap them, onto the hotbar, or out of the window to drop it. The right-click menu is gone.
• What you wear now has its own frame beside the bag: the camera turns to your character and stands you in it, wearing your real gear. Drag gear into the frame to put it on; the right slot lights up while you drag.
• Taking gear off needs a free box in your Equip tab.

New: the Keeper
• A new NPC in every town: saves your return point, opens your Storage, and teleports you between towns.
• Storage is a grid, beside your bag. Double-click moves all of a stack; Ctrl + double-click moves one; or drag between the two.
• Butterfly Wing (back to your save point) and Fly Wing (a random spot on the map you are on) are now in the game.

New: Auto-Combat
• Press T (or open System ▸ Auto-Combat) and your character hunts on its own — choose Standing, Radius or Free Roam.
• Auto-Skills: pick up to four skills to cast automatically, even ones not on your hotbar.
• Auto-Potion: drinks a health or mana potion when you fall below the percentage you set.
• Auto-Loot with a loot filter: choose which kinds of items go straight to your bag, and the rarest drop chance worth taking.

Chat
• Shift-click any item to put it in your chat line. Send it, and anyone can point at it to see its tooltip, in every kind of chat, private messages included.

Interface
• The chosen tab in every window is now filled in, so it stands out.
• Floating text has its black outline again: damage numbers, names, the kill combo, zone titles and battle notices.
• That outline is now solid black, so floating text reads over any ground.

Items & Shops
• Fixed: with more than 40 different items, the newest ones no longer go missing from the All tab.
• Each bag tab (Equip, Use, Material, Etc) now holds up to 24 entries. A stack counts as one, and what you wear counts in Equip.
• You can carry up to 2000 weight, plus 30 for every point of STR. What you wear counts too.
• When a tab is full or something is too heavy, it stays on the ground (or in the shop) and the chat tells you why. Taking a pile out of storage takes as many as you can carry.
• Quest rewards always arrive, even past your limits — the chat tells you when your bag is over.
• The bag shows how full the open tab is, and your weight against your limit.
• Item names are now coloured by rarity.
• Shops now have Buyback — get back what you sold by mistake.
• Folding and Quenching now work on gear you're wearing.
• Used-up consumables stay on your hotbar, shown in red, ready for when you restock.

Combat
• New kill combo: chain kills to raise your combo, and every combo step increases the EXP and zeny you earn.
• New EXP per hour and zeny per hour counters.
• New Combat Log tab in the chat window.
• Mobs no longer vanish in tall grass: once a mob has attacked you, or you've damaged it, it shows as a blue shape through grass and anything else in the way.

Map & Travel
• The zone view now labels every portal with where it leads — click one to jump the view to that zone.
• Click any spot on the map to draw a guide on the ground leading there, even across zones.
• The zone view's mob list now shows how many of each mob are in the zone.
• The zone name now flashes on every map change, in the colour of its map type.
• Invisible walls now close off the edges and corners of every zone, so you can no longer step off the world.
• Dungeons are no longer boxed in by generated walls.

title: A new launcher
text: The launcher has a new look and now keeps itself up to date. If you already have the game, open your launcher as usual and press Start once: instead of the game, a small window downloads the new launcher (about 100 MB), which opens by itself and keeps your game without downloading it again. If your launcher says "Access to the path … is denied", download it again from the website. The Uninstall button in the new launcher removes the game from your computer.

title: Every weapon in 3D
text: The weapons are now 3D models held in your character's hands. The greatsword, warhammer, spear, bow, dagger, katar, staff, wand, sword, axe, shuriken, scythe and sniper each have their own model and their own way of being held, and each has its own place on your body when it is put away.

title: Choose your hair
text: Character creation has a new Hair picker: step through 13 hairstyles, or pick no hair. When your character has hair, the Colours row gains one more swatch, and you paint the hair any colour with the same picker you use for the clothes.

title: Headgear you can see
text: A hat, helmet or hood worn in the Head slot now shows on your 3D character with its real shape, and every other player sees it too. Full helmets and the hood hide your hair. Other hats cover it where they sit, so only the hair hanging below shows, and headbands leave it whole.

title: Quests arrive
text: Open the Quests window with J: Tutorial, Main Story and Side Quests. New characters are given "Your First Gear", where Gunnar the Smith walks you through forging, folding and wearing your first sword, chainmail and sabatons. Torvald, the off-duty raider who wanders Lastline, has a side quest: defeat 10 Ploplings in the field west of town. Follow a quest and arrows on the ground lead you to its next step, and the route shows on your minimap and in the new Map window (M).

title: Fenwick opens his shop
text: Fenwick the Tool Dealer in Lastline sells healing potions and antidotes, one or ten at a time, and buys anything that has a sell value. Your gold finally has somewhere to go.

title: A three-row hotbar
text: The hotbar is now 3 rows of 9: F1 to F9, 1 to 9, and a third row on keys you choose in Settings. Any slot can hold a skill, an item or a piece of gear. Every ultimate now waits 40 seconds after any ultimate is cast, on top of its own cooldown.

title: Skills are bought with mastery points
text: Every weapon mastery level gives you one mastery point. Spend points in the Skills window (K) to learn a skill and raise its level, up to 10, 5 or 1 depending on the skill. Each level after the first adds 5% to the skill's numbers. Characters made before this change get all their points back to spend.

title: Saved characters
text: Beat a normal monster or an elite and there is a 15% chance it turns back into a character for 30 seconds. One that never fights pays you gold, an ally fights at your side, and a rebel fights everyone and drops better loot. Monsters no longer drop gold when they die.

title: The launcher
text: The game now comes with a launcher. It downloads the whole game the first time, then only the files that changed, and starts the game when you press Start.

title: Hills, cliffs and rain that pools
text: The fields rise and fall in hills, with rock cliffs along some roads and slopes up onto the high ground. When it rains, puddles form on level ground and lakes fill the hollows and spill downhill, the same for every player on the map.

title: A whole world
text: The world is now three regions: 75 maps plus Lastline, with cities, towns, fields and dungeon floors, and every place has a name.

title: Forging, elites and shadows
text: Make your own gear: forge it, fold it, quench it for a better grade, write stats on it with Ink, or take it apart for half of what went into it. Monsters are now normals, elites and shadows, and each of the fourteen shadows calls an elite to its side.
